justification: Adds triggers on report_audit_trail and dcp_chapter_registry and makes the paid conveyancing report refuse delivery when its audit record cannot be written. Critical: a wrong trigger could block every paid report or void citations wholesale.

pre_impl.existing_data: report_audit_trail: 10 columns, 887 rows, unique created_at, id default gen_random_uuid(), no triggers, 0 conveyancing rows. dcp_chapter_registry has only trg_dcr_updated_at; 559 active r2 paths. PG 17.6 with sha256(). conveyancing_cache report_ids: 15 of 15 are UUIDs.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed the paid report already wrote an audit row; it never called log_audit_trail. Assumed the audit trail was append-only in the database; it was append-only by docstring only.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Additive columns and triggers; the 887 existing audit rows are chained once in created_at order. No existing writer updates or deletes audit rows (grep: 0).
pre_impl.external_source_error: If the audit insert fails, the paid report returns HTTP 503 and nothing is uploaded; satellite pipelines keep the old non-blocking behaviour.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend type changes; the Next.js route already maps a non-OK response to a 502 PDF generation failed.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A database outage now stops paid reports visibly (503) instead of delivering them unrecorded. A chapter PDF change hides that chapter's clauses until the next verdict run, never shows them unchecked.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a paid report can be delivered without its audit record, the record omits a setback's verdict or source PDF, a writer ignores a changed source PDF, or any audit row was edited, deleted or inserted out of order
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 5 mutants (required raise off, audit call removed, id check off, source dropped, path ignored) each fail 1 test.

functions.name: conveyancing_evidence
functions.input: the report's fetch_dcp_setbacks dict, its LEP clauses, the PDF sha256 and the R2 key
functions.output: intermediate_calculations listing each setback shown with clause, verdict and checked-against PDF, plus a summary with the file fingerprint
functions.if_none: no setbacks or LEP clauses gives empty lists and zero counts, never an exception

functions.name: _write_conveyancing_audit
functions.input: the PDF request, resolved address and coordinates, the built PDF path and the shown setbacks
functions.output: one required report_audit_trail row written before the PDF is uploaded to storage
functions.if_none: an AuditTrailError becomes HTTP 503 and the report is not delivered to the customer

functions.name: plan_writes
functions.input: new verdicts, the chapter PDF each was judged on, and the stored (status, source) pairs
functions.output: (id, status, source) for every row whose verdict or judged PDF changed since the last run
functions.if_none: an unknown verdict raises ValueError before any write reaches the database

functions.name: main
functions.input: the live report_audit_trail rows ordered by chain_seq and the database digest function
functions.output: exit 0 when every link and digest holds, 1 naming broken rows, 2 when it cannot check
functions.if_none: an empty table verifies as intact with zero rows and exits 0

queries.purpose: void verdicts when a chapter PDF changes
queries.where_clause: council and chapter_key match NEW, is_current, citation_status IS NOT NULL (setbacks: not external)
whole table ordered by chain_seq (the chain is global by design)
lga = %s AND is_current AND needs_review not true (unchanged); adds id and citation_source_path

break_it.scenario: Two paid reports finish at the same moment and insert audit rows concurrently
break_it.what_happens: both could read the same previous row and fork the hash chain
break_it.how: the insert trigger takes pg_advisory_xact_lock before reading the last row_hash; chain_seq is unique

break_it.scenario: The database is down at the moment a customer buys a conveyancing report
break_it.what_happens: previously the report was delivered with no audit record at all
break_it.how: log_audit_trail(required=True) raises; the endpoint returns 503 before uploading

break_it.scenario: A council publishes a new PDF and the post-publish verdict re-check then fails
break_it.what_happens: old proven verdicts would keep showing clauses judged on the superseded plan
break_it.how: the registry trigger nulls that chapter's verdicts in the same transaction as the path change
break_it.repro: migrations/078_evidence_trail.sql dcp_chapter_registry_void_citations: change r2_current_path, then citation_status for its rows reads NULL

break_it.scenario: Someone edits or deletes an audit row directly in the database to hide what a report showed
break_it.what_happens: the change would be invisible to anyone reading the audit trail later
break_it.how: UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE triggers refuse it; if they are dropped, verify_audit_chain fails nightly

break_it.scenario: A caller sends a report id that is not a UUID to the paid conveyancing endpoint
break_it.what_happens: the required audit insert would fail only after the whole PDF was built
break_it.how: is_report_id is checked before any work and returns 400

break_it.scenario: The setback evidence read runs before migration 078 adds citation_source_path
break_it.what_happens: a direct column reference would raise and drop every setback from every report
break_it.how: fetch_dcp_setbacks reads it through to_jsonb(row)->>'citation_source_path', NULL when absent; the evidence then records no source rather than failing

real_layer_exempt.services/conveyancing.py: the only DB write added goes through audit_trail.log_audit_trail; a real-layer test would create a permanent, undeletable audit row in production. The live chain is checked by tests/test_verify_audit_chain_real_db.py.
real_layer_exempt.services/audit_trail.py: every real insert is permanent by design (append-only triggers); the chain itself is verified live by tests/test_verify_audit_chain_real_db.py.

post_merge.db_reset: Apply migrations/078 BEFORE merge, then re-run both verdict writers with --apply (they now record the judged PDF)
post_merge.manual_verify: Generate one paid conveyancing report, then run python scripts/verify_audit_chain.py and read its audit row (pipeline_name conveyancing).
